vectors.description: The worker presents its grant and the planner's grant above it, and nothing is revoked.
vectors.rule: A chain whose every grant verifies, links to its parent and is unrevoked at observed_at, held by its last delegate, carries authority.

vectors.description: The organisation revokes the planner's grant at 12:00 and the worker presents its child grant at 13:00.
vectors.rule: A presented chain fails when any grant in it is revoked, so a revocation cuts off every grant beneath the revoked one and nothing beside or above it.

vectors.description: The same revocation, and the relying party observed the worker's presentation at 11:00, before it took effect.
vectors.rule: A revocation applies to a presentation the relying party observed at or after the revocation's effective_at; observed_at comes from the relying party's signature, never from the presenter.

vectors.description: The planner revokes the worker's grant and the sibling presents its own grant from the same planner.
vectors.rule: A presented chain fails when any grant in it is revoked, so a revocation cuts off every grant beneath the revoked one and nothing beside or above it.

vectors.description: The organisation revokes the planner's grant and the sub-worker, two levels below, presents its chain.
vectors.rule: A presented chain fails when any grant in it is revoked, so a revocation cuts off every grant beneath the revoked one and nothing beside or above it.

vectors.description: The planner revokes the worker's grant and the planner presents its own grant.
vectors.rule: A presented chain fails when any grant in it is revoked, so a revocation cuts off every grant beneath the revoked one and nothing beside or above it.

vectors.description: A revocation issued at 14:00 states it took effect at 10:00, and the presentation was observed at 13:00.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a revocation applies from its stated effective_at even when it was issued later, as an X.509 invalidity date does; this favours containment over a relying party's reliance on the earlier state.

vectors.description: The sibling signs a revocation of the worker's grant and the worker presents.
vectors.rule: Only the issuer of the revoked grant, or an issuer above it in the presented chain, has standing to revoke it; a revocation signed by anyone else is ignored.

vectors.description: The organisation revokes the planner's grant without stating grounds and the worker presents.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a revocation from a principal with standing that states no grounds still stops the authority, and the reason names the missing record field.

vectors.description: The worker, cut off by the revocation of the planner's grant, files a dispute at 12:30 and presents at 13:00 with no resolution.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a dispute filed by an affected principal, including one cut off by the cascade, does not suspend the revocation; until a resolution signed by a principal with standing exists, the reason says the dispute is open.

vectors.description: The planner disputes, the organisation resolves the dispute in its favour and issues a replacement grant, and the planner presents the replacement.
vectors.rule: A revocation is irreversible; a restoration is a new grant, which carries authority from its own issuance and does not revive the revoked grant.

vectors.description: After the restoration the planner presents the old, revoked grant.
vectors.rule: A revocation is irreversible, so the revoked grant stays revoked after the dispute is resolved in the principal's favour.

vectors.description: After the restoration the worker presents its old grant under the planner's replacement grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a restoration does not cascade; every principal cut off by the revocation needs its own grant re-issued under the replacement, because its old grant still names the revoked parent.

vectors.description: The planner re-issues the worker's grant under the replacement and the worker presents the new chain.
vectors.rule: A grant re-issued under the replacement grant forms a chain of its own and carries authority.

vectors.description: The organisation resolves the worker's dispute by confirming the revocation, and the worker presents.
vectors.rule: A resolution that confirms the revocation closes the dispute, and the revocation stands.

vectors.description: The worker signs a resolution of its own dispute that restores the grant, and presents.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a resolution counts only when its signer has standing to revoke the grant, so a disputing principal cannot resolve its own dispute.

vectors.description: The planner revokes the worker's grant from 12:00, the organisation revokes it from 15:00, and the worker presents at 13:00.
vectors.rule: When several revocations with standing name one grant, the earliest effective_at applies.

vectors.description: The worker's grant was edited after the planner signed it.
vectors.rule: A record counts only when its signature verifies under the key the registry bound to its signer; a grant on the presented chain that fails is named.

vectors.description: A revocation of the planner's grant names the organisation and is signed by a key the registry never bound to it.
vectors.rule: A revocation whose signature does not verify counts as absent, so a forged revocation stops nothing.

vectors.description: The worker signs its presentation and the relying party does not.
vectors.rule: A presentation needs the presenter's signature and the relying party's signature; the relying party's signature is what fixes observed_at.

vectors.description: The sub-worker presents its grant directly under the planner's grant, leaving out the worker's.
vectors.rule: Each grant's parent is the grant before it in the chain and its issuer is that grant's delegate.

vectors.description: The planner issues a top-level grant to the worker on its own authority.
vectors.rule: The first grant of a chain must be issued by a root the policy trusts.

vectors.description: One record file in the set is not JSON.
vectors.rule: A record that is not a DSSE envelope over a JSON object of a known type gives no verdict.

vectors.description: agent-v1 is re-registered as agent-v2 with a link signed by both keys and the registry, agent-v1 is retired, and agent-v2 presents agent-v1's grant.
vectors.rule: A grant held by an old identifier is held by its successor when a link names old and new and carries signatures by the old identifier's key, the new identifier's key and the registry.

vectors.description: agent-v2 presents agent-v1's grant and no link names them.
vectors.rule: Without a link, a new identifier holds nothing an old identifier held.

vectors.description: The link's agent-v1 signature is made with agent-v2's key.
vectors.rule: The old identifier's signature on a link must verify under the key the registry bound to the old identifier; the new identifier cannot sign for it.

vectors.description: The link carries both agents' signatures and not the registry's.
vectors.rule: A link needs the registry's signature, because that signature is what makes linked_at trustworthy.

vectors.description: agent-v1 and a second agent, agent-b-v1, are both linked to agent-v2, which presents agent-v1's grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a link is one to one; two old identifiers linked to one new one would merge two principals' authority, which needs a new grant, so it is rejected.

vectors.description: agent-v1 is linked to agent-v2 and to agent-v2b, and agent-v2 presents.
vectors.rule: Proposed: one old identifier linked to two new ones leaves the successor ambiguous, so it is rejected.

vectors.description: The registry revokes agent-v1 for key compromise at 10:05 and a link to agent-v2 is made at 10:15.
vectors.rule: A link counts only when the registry had neither retired nor revoked the old identifier at linked_at, so a key revoked for compromise cannot pass its authority on.

vectors.description: agent-v1 is linked to agent-v2, agent-v2 to agent-v3, and agent-v3 presents agent-v1's grant.
vectors.rule: Links are followed one hop at a time, and every hop is checked as a link of its own.

vectors.description: The registry revokes agent-v2 before the agent-v2 to agent-v3 link is made, and agent-v3 presents.
vectors.rule: Links are followed one hop at a time, and every hop is checked as a link of its own.

vectors.description: agent-v1 presents its own grant after the registry retired it.
vectors.rule: A presenter whose identifier the registry retired or revoked at or before observed_at holds nothing.

vectors.description: agent-v1 presents its own grant after the link and before its retirement.
vectors.rule: Proposed: an old identifier stays usable until the registry retires it; a link alone does not end it.

vectors.description: The organisation revokes agent-v1's grant and agent-v2 presents it through the link.
vectors.rule: A link carries a grant as it stands, so a revocation of the grant applies to the successor as well.

vectors.description: The agent-v1 key is lost, the registry retires agent-v1, the registry and the organisation sign a recovery record to agent-v2, and the organisation grants agent-v2 anew, which agent-v2 presents.
vectors.rule: A new grant to the recovered identifier carries authority from its own issuance.

vectors.description: After the same recovery, agent-v2 presents agent-v1's grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a recovery record carries history, not authority; a grant reaches a new identifier only through a link signed by the old key, or through a new grant.

vectors.description: The recovery record carries the registry's signature and not the organisation's, and agent-v2 presents its new grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a recovery record needs the registry's signature and the Responsible entity's, so the registry alone cannot move an agent's history, and a presenter named by a recovery record that fails is refused because its history cannot be resolved.

vectors.description: The registry registered agent-v2 with a software attestation digest that differs from agent-v1's, and agent-v2 presents its new grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a recovery counts only when the registry registered the old and the new identifier to the same Responsible entity with the same software attestation digest.

vectors.description: The registry revokes agent-v1 for key compromise, a recovery record names agent-v2, and agent-v2 presents agent-v1's grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: a recovery never restores authority, including authority the registry removed by revoking the old identifier for compromise.

vectors.description: The registry revokes agent-v1 for key compromise, a recovery record names agent-v2, and the organisation grants agent-v2 anew, which agent-v2 presents.
vectors.rule: Proposed: adverse records of the old identifier (an identifier revocation, a revocation of a grant made to it, its disputes and their resolutions) resolve from the successor through the recovery record, and the acceptance names that history.

vectors.description: agent-v1's grant was revoked, agent-v1 disputed the revocation and the organisation confirmed it; after the key is lost and recovered to agent-v2, agent-v2 presents a new grant.
vectors.rule: Proposed: adverse records of the old identifier (an identifier revocation, a revocation of a grant made to it, its disputes and their resolutions) resolve from the successor through the recovery record, and the acceptance names that history.
